Detection probability of the whole array, per listening day

Source: R/system_de.R
system_de.Rd

For each water cell and each day, the probability that at least k listening receivers detect one transmission from the cell, treating the receivers as independent given the cell. With k = 1 this is one minus the product over listening receivers of one minus their detection probability. The station effects in sigma are not integrated here: the result is the array's coverage under the curve as given. Pedersen et al. (2014) define the coverage of a grid cell for a sensor network the same way, from the product over sensors of one minus each sensor's detection probability.

Usage

system_de(
  field,
  listening,
  k = 1,
  transmissions = 1,
  format = c("table", "raster")
)

Arguments

field

A de_field().

listening

A data frame with one row per receiver and day: a date column (Date), and the field's key column (station_id or receiver_serial) or, for a field keyed by station, receiver_serial together with the deployment lookup of the field. A day on which a serial moves goes to its later deployment; a recovery day with no later deployment of that serial goes to the station it left. An optional logical listening column drops the rows that are not TRUE, and an optional status column, as detqc::audit_listening() writes it, says why; see Details for a day with no listening row. The list list(deployments = , days = ) that detqc::as_detfield_input() returns as listening is also taken: its days table is used.

k

The number of receivers that must detect the transmission; at most the number of receivers the field holds.

transmissions

The number of transmissions the tag sends in a bin, one whole number of at least 1. The default, 1, gives the probability for one transmission.

format

"table" for a data frame with columns date, cell, p and n_listening; "raster" for a terra::SpatRaster with one layer per day, named by date.

Value

A data frame or a SpatRaster, as format says. p is the probability for one transmission, or for a bin of transmissions

transmissions. A receiver in listening that the field does not hold is an error on any row, listening or not, including the rows of a day that is left out. A field built for one date (de_field(date = )) scored against a listening table with no row on that date gives a warning, because the result takes its dates from listening.

Details

With transmissions above 1, the same probability for a bin in which the tag sent that many transmissions: each receiver hears at least one of them with probability 1 - (1 - p)^transmissions, the transmissions being independent given the cell, and at least k receivers must each hear one. This is the probability that the bin is detected from the cell, which is the weight sample_available() needs for availability in hourly bins: an hour holds 3600 / mean delay transmissions, 24 at the 150 s mean delay of the Stoney tags. A spread of a receiver's detection probability between hours (sigma$station_hour) makes the transmissions of one hour fail together, and the probability lower than the value given here; it is not integrated. transmissions = 1 gives exactly the per-transmission result.

Days that share the same set of listening receivers are computed once. A day with fewer listening receivers than k gives 0 in every cell, and every value lies in 0 to 1: the sum behind it is clamped, so rounding never gives a probability below 0.

Days with no listening receiver. A day on which every row has listening = FALSE and a status of "off" or "deaf" gives 0 in every cell and n_listening 0: the receivers' own logs show that none of them could hear. Any other day without a listening row is left out of the result: a status of "not_downloaded", "reference_silent" or "silent_run", a missing status column, or listening = NA. On such a day a receiver may have been listening with its data missing, and a 0 would misstate the coverage. A date with no row in listening is also left out. On a day with at least one listening row, the rows that are not listening are dropped whatever their status, so a "not_downloaded" receiver is left out and the coverage comes from the receivers that listened.

References

Pedersen, M. W., Burgess, G. and Weng, K. C. (2014). A quantitative approach to static sensor network design. Methods in Ecology and Evolution, 5, 1043-1051. doi:10.1111/2041-210X.12255

See also

de_field(); sample_available(), which takes the per-bin table.

Examples

# The Stoney example: Stoney Lake (100 m cells, land NA) and 70 receivers.
tif <- system.file("extdata", "stoney_depth.tif", package = "detfield")
grid <- terra::rast(tif)
curve <- de_logistic(d50 = c(250, 750), d05 = c(500, 1500), depth = c(1, 35))
# Pairs beyond 2 km are left out: there every receiver hears less than 1e-4.
dist <- water_distances(grid, stoney_track$receivers, max_distance = 2000)
field <- de_field(dist, curve)
#> 194 of 7,669 receiver-cell pairs with p >= 0.05 have land on the
#>   straight line between them; with blocked = 0 the curve is read on
#>   them as if the line were clear. See `blocked` in ?de_model.
# All 70 stations listen on 1 June; S005 to S009 are silent on 2 June.
stations <- stoney_track$receivers$station_id
listening <- data.frame(
  station_id = c(stations, setdiff(stations, sprintf("S%03d", 5:9))),
  date = as.Date(rep(c("2024-06-01", "2024-06-02"), c(70, 65)))
)
cover <- system_de(field, listening)
tapply(cover$p, cover$date, mean)
#> 2024-06-01 2024-06-02 
#>  0.4740107  0.4405511 
system_de(field, listening, format = "raster")
#> class       : SpatRaster 
#> dimensions  : 127, 168, 2  (nrow, ncol, nlyr)
#> resolution  : 100, 100  (x, y)
#> extent      : 720304, 737104, 4929241, 4941941  (xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax)
#> coord. ref. : WGS 84 / UTM zone 17N (EPSG:32617) 
#> source(s)   : memory
#> names       : 2024-06-01, 2024-06-02 
#> min values  :  0.0000000,  0.0000000 
#> max values  :  0.9675785,  0.9675785 
# Per hour: 24 transmissions at the tags' 150 s mean delay
hourly <- system_de(field, listening, transmissions = 24)
tapply(hourly$p >= 0.95, hourly$date, mean)
#> 2024-06-01 2024-06-02 
#>  0.7768784  0.7411789
